messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Add Tag via R
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
there is currently no built-in function in camtrapR to achieve this.
Since you can extract the UserComment with recordTable(), you can call Exiftool from R to write the content of usercomment to the HierarchicalSubject tag though (which digiKam reads).

Here's the rough idea (for assigning the value in the column UserComment of the record table to a tag "Species" in the HierarchicalSubject field in the image metadata:

species_tag <- paste("Species", rec$UserComment, sep = "|")
exif_call <- paste0('exiftool -hierarchicalsubject+="', species_tag, '" ', file.path(rec$Directory, rec$FileName))

system(exif_call)  # for one image
sapply(exif_call, system)   # for multiple images

system(paste('exiftool -HierarchicalSubject ', file.path(rec$Directory[1], rec$FileName[1])))  # for checking

It is quite clumsy and very slow since it calls exiftool for each image separately. Performance can be increased by parallelization (e.g. parSapply).

Alternatively, one can probably achieve the same with Exiftool for entire directories instead of files, either from the command line or within R using a system call.
One can copy values from one metadata tag to another (see e.g. here <https://exiftool.org/exiftool_pod.html#COPYING%20EXAMPLES>), but here we need to copy it as structured information (e.g. with a prefix "Species|" in HierarchicalSubject). I don't know how to do that in Exiftool and don't have code to share. The Exiftool forum (https://exiftool.org/forum/) might be a good place to find help on that though, and there were some similar questions in the past already. If there is a solution please share, then I can maybe add it to camtrapR in the future.

Either way, in digiKam one needs to click "Read metadata from file to database" to see the newly assigned tags.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Announcement: Shiny dashboard in camtrapR
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I am pleased to share with you a new and exciting development in camtrapR: a Shiny dashboard for summarizing, viewing and analyzing camera trapping data sets. It is available in the GitHub version via the new function:
surveyDashboard().

The dashboard has 10 pages to:
provide key information about surveys
show interactive maps of camera trap locations and species detections
easily and flexibly fit single-species occupancy models with unmarked (including automatically created plots of species responses to covariates and model selection tables)
visualize single and two-species activity patterns

Install from GitHub to give it a try:
remotes::install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", build_vignettes = TRUE)

I'd be happy to hear feedback to further improve the dashboard and make it more versatile and useful for you.

Thank you for using camtrapR.
Best regards,
Jürgen Niedballa

Hi Michael,
internally the model operates on the logit scale, so the beta parameters refer to the logit scale. The  plot_effects() function simply backtransforms the logit values to probability internally and only presents you the probability values.

To answer your question, there are several ways to get occupancy probability for species/station combinations.

Please see the post linked below for solutions to your question. I'd recommend to go with the first solution here, it's by far the easiest and I guess I should change the function to make the model return psi by default.

https://groups.google.com/g/camtrapr/c/IcXsF_x1I6g

A third solution would be to use the formula as you suggested and then backtransform, e.g. using invlogit() from the secr package, but that's troublesome and more error prone.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hello Michael,
It's hard to say without the data and the model, but it suggests that there is unexplained variation in the data for those species.

Some possible causes:
- detection process if affected by variables not included in model (spatial and / or temporal)
- the actual detection probabilities of those common species might be higher than what the random effect structure of the model permits (since the random effect ties the species estimates together via its community mean + standard deviation)

Things to try:
- Royle-Nichols model (often works well in such situations by allowing more variation in the detection process, via parameter model = "RN"
- longer occasions
- additional covariates on detection
- include species-station random effect on detection (can affect other estimates strongly and absorbs a lot of the overall variation in the data, leaving little for the occupancy covariates while being hard to interpret, use with caution)

In any case it would make sense to examine the data to figure out what is unusual about the detections of these species. That may give cues about how to fix the lack of fit.

Best regards,
Jürgen
